title: Make dispatch-log append failure-atomic
prompt: Make DispatchLog#append failure-atomic for one local process. Build the complete next JSON document before replacing the current log. Write it to a uniquely named temporary file in the same directory whose basename starts with .<log-basename>.tmp-, then replace the log with File.rename only after the write completes. If writing or renaming fails, preserve the prior log byte-for-byte, remove the temporary file, and re-raise the original exception. Preserve DispatchLog.new(path), successful append behavior, and entries. Add focused tests for a partial temporary-file write failure and cleanup. Do not add concurrency handling or recovery of temp files left by a killed process.

workflows: read and build the next document
rename only after the write succeeds
clean the temporary file and re-raise on failure
invariants: a failed append preserves the prior log byte-for-byte
a failed append leaves no task-owned temporary file
a successful append remains readable through entries
rubric.impact_question: Why does same-directory rename improve local failure atomicity but not provide durability against every filesystem or process failure?
accepted_alternatives: write a unique same-directory temporary path and File.rename it over the log

runtime_only_if_observed: the direct-overwrite attempt corrupted the prior log
the observed failure that caused the replacement-boundary revision
